guards.what: EV-3: Group's two `CardCmd.TransformToRandom(item, base.Rng, ...)` calls (MorphicGrove.cs:50) -- events/morphic_grove.py:44 calls run.transform_card with no pick_rng, so run.py:457-458 falls back to `self.rng.choice` rolls on the sim's shared run RNG (`self.rng`) where C# rolls on the per-event `base.Rng`
guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-3, one verdict at every site (rule 3). Each C# EventModel gets its own Rng seeded from the run seed + event id, and the sim already models it: Event.__init__ builds `self.event_rng` from make_event_rng(seed, ID) for string-seeded runs (events/base.py:84-88), and 6 modules branch on it. EXECUTED (`py tools/audit/event_probes.py eventrng`): 28 of the 34 event modules that roll anything roll ONLY on `self.rng`. LIVE for the parity path that the conformance harness grades -- a shared-rng draw both takes a number the game never takes off that stream and fails to advance the event stream, desyncing the rest of the run. In legacy (RL) mode both are the same random.Random, so the observable is parity-only -- which is an exercised sim mode, not an unreachable one.

guards.what: EV-10 (site): run.transformable_cards (run.py:364-366) reuses the REMOVAL predicate for the TRANSFORM screen, so Quest cards are offered where CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForTransformation (CardSelectCmd.cs:487) filters `c.Type != CardType.Quest && c.IsTransformable`. This unit calls it twice -- once as the IsAllowed gate (events/morphic_grove.py:30) and once as the GROUP selection (events/morphic_grove.py:41)
guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-10, one verdict at every transformable_cards() site (rule 3), stated in full on event/trial -- not re-verdicted here. Recorded on this unit because event/trial named it "the sharpest case" on a claim that turns out to be false, and the correction belongs where the claim was about. THE GATE IS FINE: MorphicGrove.cs:26 counts `c.IsTransformable`, which for a Deck card is `!Eternal` (CardModel.cs:739-750) with no Quest clause, so the game counts Quest cards toward the >= 2 exactly as the sim does. EXECUTED (ad-hoc, repo root): deck [strike, spoils_map] with gold 100 -- sim is_allowed True, game count 2 -> True. The two gates AGREE, and the earlier "a Quest card can make the sim offer a map node the game would not" was never true. THE SELECTION IS NOT FINE, and it is LIVE: on that same deck the sim's screen offers ['strike','spoils_map'] where the game's offers ['strike'], and because GROUP passes `new CardSelectorPrefs(prompt, 2)` -- MinSelect == MaxSelect == 2, so RequireManualConfirmation is false (CardSelectorPrefs.cs:68-78) -- the game auto-takes its whole 1-card list (CardSelectCmd.cs:493-495) and transforms ONE card, while the sim transforms TWO and destroys the Quest card outright. Reachable with ported content: the three ported Quest cards are byrdonis_egg, lantern_key and spoils_map (event/trial's `py audit/tools/event_probes_b.py quest`).
